texts: good. the crowd, its nightmoth members, the gathering at the Harbor Row and the Year 1 / day 258 dating all land as stated. One caveat that is ours and not yours: we have no day-of-year time term, so "day 258" occupies the day-of-month slot and dated events in this world will not automatically order against each other — no rewrite of the sentence would fix that.
good. the three sky-cats come through as a counted group with the descent and its cliff-spire source, plus a fireable per-cat rule, so a sky-cat named later inherits its own descent.
good. the hunt reuses the same sky-cat group and the same nightmoth crowd as the earlier sentences, and the post-verbal "at the Harbor Row" attaches to the hunting, as the wording allows.

bad: here "at the Harbor Row" sits inside the subject noun phrase, so it says where the crowd is — but the parse hangs it on the shrinking instead, asserting a place for the shrinking you never stated while losing the crowd's stated location. Give the location its own clause: "The nightmoth crowd was at the Harbor Row, and it shrank."
good. the count of twenty-four, the lantern of the Harbor Station as the place, and "before the hunt" ordered against the hunt event of sentence 3 all land.
good. mirrors sentence 5 — nine nightmoths, the same lantern, and "after the hunt" recorded as the hunt preceding this count.
good. the notes are a group of notes brought into being by the writing, and "about the hunt" links back to the same hunt event.
